To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentration of CO2 and DOC and major and trace element concentrations in supra-permafrost soil waters decrease with increasing ALT, decreasing annual temperature, and increasing permafrost cover.
the concentration of CO2, dissolved carbon, alkaline earth elements, and trace metals in supra-permafrost peat soils of WSL increases northwards and decreases with permafrost coverage and ALT.
the permafrost coverage and climate warming may have a significant effect on the concentration of CO2, carbon and trace elements in the supra-permafost water of the WSL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of climate warming on the carbon cycle and GHGs dynamics, which are important factors for global change.
the fate of the WSL peatlands under climate change and permafrost thaw, which is a key issue for understanding of the global carbon cycle.
the fate of carbon and elements under permafrost thaw, which may be important in the context of climate change and the global carbon cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the climate change scenario of permafrost warming and thaw will decrease the concentration of CO2, DOC and many TE in supra-permafrost peat waters.
the permafrost thaw will decrease the intensity of CO2, DOC and TE mobilizations from the peat soil to the supra-permastrofrost water and to rivers and lakes of the WSL.
climate warming and permafrost thaw may decrease the CO-DOC-Mn-Ni-Cu-V-Mo export from peat soil and vegetation litter of the WSL, which may have a positive effect on the global warming.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the climate change and permafrost thaw may decrease the CO-2, DOC, alkaline earth metal, and TE concentrations in supra-permafrost soil pore waters of the WSL, which may decrease their export to lakes and rivers.
the WSL is an extremely heterogeneous environment with a complex pattern of soil and supra-permafrost pore water chemistry.

climate warming and permafrost thaw may result in a decrease in CO2, DOC and many major and minor elements in supra-permafrost peat soil waters, which in turn will decrease the carbon, and metal export from peatlands of the WSL to lakes and rivers and further to the Arctic ocean.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WSL peatland will continue to be a major source of DOC and GHG to the Arctic Ocean in the near future, even if the permafrost will thaw and the active layer will increase.
the permafrost thaw will not only increase the carbon emissions but will also change the geochemical composition of the soil waters.
the permafrost zone of the WSL will be an important source of DOC and TE to the Arctic Ocean, and that the permafrozen zone will be a net sink of carbon, CO2 and many TE.
